chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Habib al-Sijistani who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when He extracted the offspring of Adam (peace be upon him) from his back in order to take the covenant upon them regarding His Lordship and prophethood for every prophet, the first one for whom He took the covenant upon them — regarding his prophethood — was Muhammad ibn Abdullah (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Adam: 'Look! What do you see?' He said: So Adam (peace be upon him) looked at his offspring, and they were tiny particles that had filled the sky. Adam (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord! How abundant are my offspring! And for what purpose did You create them? So what do You want from them by taking the covenant upon them?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'That they worship Me, not associating anything with Me, and believe in My messengers and follow them.'

Adam (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord! Why do I see some of the particles greater than others, some of them have much light, some of them have little light, and some of them have no light?' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Thus have I created them, in order to test them in all their states.' Adam (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord! Will You permit me to speak?' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'Speak, for your spirit is from My Spirit, but your nature is contrary to My Being.' Adam said: 'O Lord! If only You had created them upon one likeness, one measure, one nature, one constitution, one colour, one lifespan, and equal sustenance — then some of them would not oppress others, and there would be no envy, hatred, or disagreement among them regarding anything.'

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'O Adam! By My Spirit you spoke, but by the weakness of your nature you ventured into what you have no knowledge of. I am the Creator, the All-Knowing. By My knowledge I have differentiated in their creation, and by My will My command runs among them, and to My management and My ordainment they are coming. There is no alteration in My creation. Indeed, I created the jinn and mankind only that they worship Me. And I created Paradise for those among them who obey Me, worship Me, and follow My messengers — and I do not retract. And I created the Fire for those who disbelieve in Me, disobey Me, and do not follow My messengers — and I do not retract. And I created you and your offspring not out of any need I have for you or them. Rather, I created you and created them to test you and test them — which of you excels in deed in the abode of the world, during your lifetime and before your death. For that reason I created this world and the next, life and death, obedience and disobedience, Paradise and the Fire.'

And likewise I intended in My ordainment and My management, and with My penetrating knowledge among them I differentiated between their forms, their bodies, their colours, their lifespans, their sustenance, their obedience and their disobedience. So I made among them the wretched and the fortunate, the seeing and the blind, the short and the tall, the beautiful and the ugly, the knowledgeable and the ignorant, the rich and the poor, the obedient and the disobedient, the healthy and the sick, and those with disabilities and those with no affliction. So the healthy looks at the one with the affliction and praises Me for his own well-being. And the one with the affliction looks at the healthy and supplicates to Me and asks Me to grant him well-being, and is patient in My trial, so I reward him generously from My gifts. And the rich looks at the poor and praises Me and thanks Me. And the poor looks at the rich and supplicates to Me and asks Me. And the believer looks at the disbeliever and praises Me for guiding him.

For that reason I created them — to test them in ease and adversity, in what I grant them well-being and in what I afflict them, in what I give them and in what I withhold from them. And I am Allah, the King, the All-Powerful. It is Mine to execute all that I have ordained according to what I have managed. And it is Mine to change whatever I will of that to whatever I will, and to bring forward what I had delayed, and to delay what I had brought forward. And I am Allah, the Doer of whatever I will. I am not questioned about what I do, and I shall question My creation about what they do.'

key_terms.الابتلاء: Trial, testing; divine test through worldly circumstances
key_terms.الذر: Tiny particles, atoms; the primordial form of all human souls
key_terms.الذرية: Offspring, descendants; here the pre-worldly particles extracted from Adam's back
key_terms.الكينونة: Divine Being, existence; refers to God's essential nature
key_terms.الميثاق: The primordial covenant, the Covenant of Alast (referring to Quran 7:172)

ai.seo_question: What is the hadith about the covenant of Alast and Adam's offspring as particles of light in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates a profound cosmological account of the primordial covenant (mithaq), in which God extracted all of Adam's offspring as particles of light from his back, took their covenant acknowledging His Lordship and the prophethood of all prophets — beginning with Muhammad (SAWW) — and revealed to Adam the divine wisdom behind human diversity. When Adam questioned why God created humans with different qualities of light, lifespans, and provisions, God replied that He tests humanity through this very diversity: the healthy praise Him when they see the afflicted, the afflicted turn to Him in prayer, the rich thank Him when they see the poor, and the believer thanks Him for guidance. This hadith directly addresses 7:172 (the Day of Alast), the divine purpose in creation (51:56), and divine sovereignty (21:23), grounding the Shia theology of divine justice and free will within the framework of pre-eternal covenant.
